summary: USB-C dock NIC offload suppresses DAD causing WireGuard tunnel to bind to stale interface and break access
description:
Issue summary: Several employees reported loss of access to internal services (git, k8s API, internal console) immediately after connecting a corporate USB-C dock while WireGuard-based VPN was active. Impact: Affected users temporarily lost ability to reach internal endpoints; SSH sessions dropped; tooling timed out. Scope: Reported by 6 users in SFO office and remote users with the same dock model (CalDigit TS4 clone).

Observed behavior: When the dock's Ethernet interface enumerates the host OS, Duplicate Address Detection (DAD) on Windows appears to be suppressed by the dock's NIC offload/firmware feature. WireGuard process continues to keep the tunnel bound to the original Wi-Fi virtual interface route (index), but Windows reassigns metrics so traffic prefers the dock interface. This results in outbound packets for internal ranges leaving over the dock NIC without being encapsulated, causing asymmetric routing and dropped connections to internal services.

Initial detection: Support triaged via #internal-networking and captured device diagnostics and logs from affected endpoints. No platform-facing incidents were triggered (no public status page events).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start WireGuard tunnel to corporate peer from Windows 11 laptop on Wi-Fi (connected to corp-ssid).
2) Establish SSH session to internal jump host.
3) Connect USB-C dock with ethernet to laptop; allow Windows to install drivers and bring interface up.
4) Observe SSH hangs/drop within 10-30s; run `ipconfig /all` and `route print` to observe route metric changes.
5) Verify WireGuard interface still marked up (wg show).
6) Reproduce: disconnect dock -> traffic returns to tunnel and SSH resumes.
logs: Mar 12 09:42:13 host-msa WireGuard[pid=2345]: peer x.x.x.x: handshake complete
Mar 12 09:42:40 host-msa NetworkChange: Ethernet0 up (ifIndex=12) metric changed -> 10
Mar 12 09:42:41 host-msa WireGuard: interface wg0 remains bound to ifIndex=15 (Wi-Fi virtual adapter)
Mar 12 09:42:41 host-msa kernel: tx packet 192.168.100.0/24 leaving via ifIndex=12 (Ethernet0) without encapsulation
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses: 1) Dock NIC firmware advertises L2 capabilities that cause OS to prefer it and suppress normal DAD causing the same IP to appear on two logical interfaces. 2) Zero-trust agent/WireGuard lacks robust rebind logic when OS interface indices/metrics change. 3) Windows route metric priority change causes unencapsulated traffic.

Findings: Captured route tables on two affected hosts show identical source IPs present on both Wi-Fi and dock interfaces for short windows. WireGuard status (`wg show`) still lists the original endpoint and interface index; however outbound packets prefer the newly created Ethernet route. The zero-trust agent does not automatically re-evaluate the preferred interface until a reconnection or network change event is triggered.

Related context: See linked INT-33109 (dock ethernet/wifi dns suffix ordering) for prior dock-related failures; also related to INT-927413 (usb-c dock multi-homing sso timeouts).
technical_analysis:
Packet captures (Wireshark) show SYNs for internal services leaving via dock NIC without WireGuard encapsulation. WireGuard's on-disk config uses a persistent interface name; Windows ifIndex changes when the dock enumerates causing the kernel route table to prefer physical Ethernet. Windows' TCP/IP stack performs weak DAD enforcement when NIC hardware offload claims to handle LLA. Driver/firmware from the dock vendor is observed to short-circuit the usual NDIS DAD messages.

Observed on: Windows 11 22H2 with vendor driver v1.12.0 and also reproduced on a MacBook running the vendor's Ethernet firmware in a separate test (Mac had different manifestation but we focused on Windows reproduction).
temporary_workaround:
- Instruct affected users to disconnect the dock before establishing WireGuard tunnel, or to reconnect the VPN after dock is attached.
- Support runbook step: `netsh interface set interface \"Ethernet 2\" metric=9999` to deprioritize the dock interface as a stopgap.
- For remote users, recommend disabling NIC offload features if driver exposes them (`ethtool` equivalent or vendor tool).
next_steps:
1) Network/endpoint teams to request vendor driver/firmware from CalDigit clone vendor and validate DAD behavior in controlled lab.
2) Endpoint team to add resilient rebind logic in zero-trust agent: detect ifIndex changes or overlapping source IPs and trigger a re-evaluation/reconnect of WireGuard. (See zt-agent PR referenced).
3) Ops to create automated health check on agent to detect interface duplication and surface telemetry to Console.
4) Communication: email to SFO floor + internal KB entry with workaround.
5) Follow up ticket for long-term fix and vendor escalation if driver is root cause.
resolution_notes:
(In Progress) Mitigation applied: Endpoint team pushed a policy to set high metric on dock ethernet for corp-managed laptops which reduced incidence by ~90% for SFO devices. Diego drafted PR to add interface-change-triggered reconnection to zero-trust agent (https://github.com/redwood-inference/zt-agent/pull/412). Vendor engagement opened; awaiting firmware build from vendor for DAD fix.

Permanent fix options under evaluation: agent-side automatic rebind vs vendor firmware fix; both paths require QA and staggered rollout.
